    Part 1: Listening comprehension



                       AN INTERVIEW WITH GOTCHA, THE MUSICAL FORCE

    In this podcast you are going to hear some new words. Read and listen to them. Make sure
    you know what they mean.

    to quote: citar textualment / citar textualmente
    prone: propens / propenso
    bouts: períodes / períodos
    harp: arpa


         Ready?
         Now read the questions on the following page. Read them carefully before listening to
    the podcast.
    [Now listen to the interview.]




2
                                                   QUESTIONS

Choose the best answer according to the recording. Only ONE answer is correct.
[3 points: 0.375 points for each correct answer. Wrong answers will be penalized by deducting 0.125 points. There is no
penalty for unanswered questions.]

                                                                                            Correcta   Incorrecta   contestada
1.   When Gotcha explains what inspired “Turning a Blind Eye”, what does
     she say is behind the feeling of defeat?
     ■ The pressure of competing with other contemporary Australian musicians.
     ■ Her inability to adapt to present-day Australian lifestyle.
     ■ Her awareness of how everyday habits lead to overconsumption.
     ■ A disappointment about how little artists care about technology.
2.   Gotcha finds it difficult to change her environmental habits because
     ■ it’s hard to know what really helps.
     ■ there is too much information, she feels overwhelmed.
     ■ she thinks no one else is making an effort.
     ■ it’s difficult to change long-established habits.
3.   How does Gotcha describe the way she sees the future?
     ■ She is idealistic most of the time, so her songs are optimistic despite
         her negative thoughts.
     ■ She alternates idealism and deep pessimism about the future, which is
         reflected in her songs.
     ■ She feels the world is as pessimistic as she is, though some people do
         want to change the world.
     ■ She is indifferent about the future, so her songs are never influenced
         by her emotions.
4.   What does touring make Gotcha aware of?
     ■ The contrast between her environmentally friendly lifestyle and that
         of other musicians.
     ■ How travelling constantly increases her environmental impact.
     ■ How certain hotels contribute to the overall carbon footprint.
     ■ How each culture approaches environmental problems differently.
5.   How does Gotcha feel about her growing success?
     ■ She thinks success always brings joy to anyone.
     ■ She fears larger projects will feel less meaningful to her.
     ■ She is afraid that fans will expect her to keep things as personal
         as they have been so far.
     ■ She believes enjoying fame will fix her environmental worries.
6.   What challenges does Gotcha mention regarding communication on
     social media as her audience grows?
     ■ She now posts more often because she feels she owes it to her new followers.
     ■ She is more aware of the diversity of her audience and how that affects
         her communication.
     ■ She prefers to post less because communication with her listeners has
         become less sustainable.
     ■ She feels that social media makes followers focus on what she says
         rather than on her music.
7.   What happens when Gotcha records an acoustic instrument note by note?
     ■ The instrument sounds the same as usual.
     ■ The resulting sound is amazing.
     ■ The instrument as such does not appear in the resulting album.
     ■ The sound of the instrument becomes angelic.
8.   Gotcha enjoys experimenting with unusual objects to create sounds because
     ■ all other artists use traditional instruments, which is uninteresting.
     ■ they help her explore a new way to make music and create more
         original musical stories.
     ■ it takes less time than recording traditional instruments.
     ■ avoiding experimentation makes her music sound like everybody else’s.

    Part 1: Listening comprehension



                    A CONVERSATION WITH YAYOI KUSAMA ON THE POWER
                                 OF ART AND EMOTIONS

    In this radio programme you are going to hear some new words. Read and listen to them.
    Make sure you know what they mean.

    art installations: instaŀlacions artístiques, creacions artístiques / instalaciones artísticas, creaciones artísticas
    polka dots: estampat de rodones / estampado de lunares
    boundless: sense límits / sin límites
    tapestry: tapís / tapiz


         Ready?
         Now read the questions on the following page. Read them carefully before listening to
    the radio programme.
    [Now listen to the interview.]




2
                                                   QUESTIONS

Choose the best answer according to the recording. Only ONE answer is correct.
[3 points: 0.375 points for each correct answer. Wrong answers will be penalized by deducting 0.125 points. There is no
penalty for unanswered questions.]

                                                                                                Espai per a la correcció
                                                                                                                      No
                                                                                           Correcta   Incorrecta   contestada
1.   How does Yayoi Kusama see the relationship between her work and the
     emotions it expresses?
     ■ The essence of her art is driven by a love for immense chaos and mystery.
     ■ Her installations aim to change viewers’ perspective on love.
     ■ The essence of her art lies in creating a collective supportive feeling.
     ■ Her work is meant to reflect the limits of love and hope.
2.   Yayoi Kusama created her “Infinity Rooms” to invite people to think about
     ■ the problem of mental illness.
     ■ the possibility of space travel.
     ■ our place in the universe.
     ■ mirrors and tapestries.
3.   In her autobiography, Yayoi Kusama mentions suffering from mental
     health problems. How has art affected her?
     ■ Art has increased her sense of despair and hopelessness.
     ■ Art has given her tools to reverse her suffering and despair.
     ■ Art has intensified her need to overcome her mental health problems.
     ■ Creating art has cancelled her positive emotions.
4.   According to the interviewer, why does Yayoi Kusama paint dots abundantly?
     ■ To portray the universe.
     ■ As a form of artistic rebellion.
     ■ To represent distress.
     ■ To create a sense of abundance.
5.   What other type of message does Kusama’s use of polka dots convey?
     ■ The dots represent how the elements of outer space are interconnected.
     ■ They serve as a visual metaphor for the chaotic nature of the universe.
     ■ Polka dots symbolize how individuals are connected.
     ■ The repetition of dots represents individuals’ everyday fighting.
6.   Why does Yayoi Kusama believe her art can surpass cultural gaps?
     ■ Because people from all walks of life visit her installations.
     ■ Because her art speaks a language that can be understood by all art
         experts.
     ■ Because her art connects people at the core of their essence as human
         beings.
     ■ Because polka dots are bound to a specific cultural audience.
7.   According to Yayoi Kusama, why did she choose to leave Japan?
     ■ Kusama was aware of her artistic identity in Japan and chose to leave
         to develop it further.
     ■ The Japanese artists did not support her because of her mental
         health issues.
     ■ The Japanese government’s restrictions on kimonos made her move.
     ■ Kusama had connections in New York that could allow her to succeed
         as an artist there.
8.   How does Yayoi Kusama see the power of art in facing global challenges?
     ■ Art has the power of eliminating global uncertainty.
     ■ Art inspires people to work together for the common good.
     ■ Art helps people see global challenges as an inevitable part of their
         future.
     ■ Art gets people to look into the past and learn from it.
